Definition: from G4862 and ἵημι (to send); to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously:-- consider, understand, be wise.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus says the good ground is the one who hears the word and understands it, and bears fruit a hundredfold, and when He asks the disciples whether they have understood all these things, they say, Yes, Lord. After the resurrection He opens their understanding that they might understand the Scriptures, and Paul says not to be unwise but to understand what the will of the Lord is. Understanding is the difference between seed on the path and seed in good ground, and it is the risen Christ who opens it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe understanding is the work of the risen Christ opening my mind to the Scriptures, and I hold that fruit follows understanding as surely as harvest follows good ground. I take the command personally: be not unwise, but understand what the will of the Lord is, and let the fruit show it.
